sections.text: Each cluster (the address it was read at under its name): ONTAP version, system health, nodes up, space used on its aggregates, NTP servers.
sections.title: Clusters

sections.text: State (green up, red down), uptime (days hours:minutes), model, version, whether the partner could take over, service processor, NVRAM battery, and the node's clock against the AAP server's. No node was read.
sections.title: Nodes

sections.text: Volumes at or above 85% used (amber) or 90% (red), and volumes offline or restricted (red), with the aggregate they are on. Volumes under 50 GB are left out (0 at or above 85%, 0 not online). Every volume is online and below 85%.
sections.title: Volumes 85% full or more, or not online

sections.text: ONTAP's health monitors by subsystem (system health subsystem show). Only the ones not OK. Every subsystem is OK.
sections.title: System health

sections.text: Each controller and disk shelf: power supplies, fans, temperature and any failed part (FRU). Problems first. No controller or shelf was read.
sections.title: Hardware: controllers and shelves

sections.text: Disks that are broken (red), rebuilding, copying or in maintenance (amber), or not assigned to a node (Low). No failed or rebuilding disk.
sections.title: Disks: failed, rebuilding or unassigned

sections.text: Spare disks per node (by home node): ONTAP rebuilds a failed disk onto a spare. No disk was read.
sections.title: Spare disks

sections.text: Data and management LIFs (IP and FC) that are down (red), not on their home port (amber; the home port under the one it is on), or disabled (blue). Every LIF is up and at home.
sections.title: Network interfaces (LIFs): down, not at home, or disabled

sections.text: Enabled Ethernet and FC ports that are not up. Red: a port in a broadcast domain (meant to be used) or an FC port that lost its link. Blue: a port with no cable or not in use. Every enabled port is up.
sections.title: Ports down

sections.text: Physical Ethernet ports with receive errors (bad frames, CRC errors among them) or CRC errors, counted since the node booted. Rising numbers mean a bad cable, SFP or switch port. No port has errors.
sections.title: Port errors (CRC)

sections.text: Every data aggregate, fullest first: the node it is on (and its home node when it is away), space used, size and available, used % (amber from 85%, red from 90%), RAID type and disks. Root aggregates are not listed (ONTAP's REST API hides them). No aggregate was read.
sections.title: Aggregates

sections.text: After a takeover or a manual move an aggregate can stay on the partner node: give it back (storage failover giveback) when the node is healthy. Every aggregate is on its home node.
sections.title: Aggregates not on their home node

sections.text: Volumes running out of inodes: when they are all used, no new file can be created, whatever the free space (volume modify -files). No volume is running out of inodes.
sections.title: Inodes (files) 85% used or more

sections.text: The volumes whose snapshots hold the most space (top 25), and any whose snapshots use more than their reserve (amber from 100% of the reserve: they spill into the volume's space). No snapshot space used.
sections.title: Snapshot space

sections.text: Relationships (read on each destination cluster) that are unhealthy (red), lagging (amber from 24 h, red from 48 h since the last good transfer), broken off, paused or uninitialized, and the transfers running now (blue): progress is the data moved so far. No relationship needs attention.
sections.title: SnapMirror

sections.text: The peer relationships SnapMirror needs: cluster peers not available, SVM peers not peered. Every peer is available.
sections.title: Cluster and SVM peers

sections.text: Storage VMs that are stopped or starting. A stopped DR destination (dp_destination) is normal (blue). Every SVM is running.
sections.title: SVMs not running

lines: c1 / svm1: not contacted - vserver cifs domain discovered-servers show -vserver svm1; to make ONTAP probe them again: vserver cifs domain discovered-servers reset-servers -vserver svm1 (a change: run it in a quiet window)
sections.text: Each SVM's CIFS server: enabled or not (red when stopped), and its domain controllers (cifs domains; ONTAP 9.10+) - OK = connected; not contacted = listed, but ONTAP has had no need to probe it (blue, never a finding, even when no DC is OK: ONTAP's normal state); not reachable = ONTAP tried it and failed (amber; said when it is a preferred DC); red = ONTAP tried every DC it lists and reached none, or the CIFS server stopped. Every DC is listed in the next table; below, the commands to look further where no DC is OK or one is not reachable.
sections.title: CIFS (SMB) servers

sections.text: Every server ONTAP lists for each SVM (DC, LDAP, KDC), with its preference and state. Not contacted (undetermined): ONTAP has not needed it - DCs in other sites or of lower preference stay so; it is not a problem. Not reachable first, then OK, then not contacted.
sections.title: CIFS domain controllers

sections.text: LUNs no host can see (not mapped to an igroup: amber - forgotten, or waiting to be deleted?) and LUNs not online (red). Every LUN is online and mapped.
sections.title: LUNs: unmapped or not online

sections.text: Certificates that expire within 60 days (amber) or 14 days (red), or have expired. CA certificates are amber at most until they expire. No certificate expires within 60 days.
sections.title: Certificates expiring

sections.text: What ONTAP's health monitors raised (system health alert show); the probable cause and what to do are in the next table, in the same order. No health alert.
sections.title: Health alerts

sections.text: ONTAP's event log (EMS): emergency, alert and error events, the same event on the same node counted once, most frequent first. No such event.
sections.title: Error events (last 24 h)
